newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end light trade barely mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end light trade barely mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended fairly light afternoon trading barely mixed.

Swiss francs popped up again just before the close as a fund re-entered and bought another 1,000 Swiss and sold as many nearby marks in a spread. The fund earlier had sold the same spread for the same size, brokers said.
The entity also was seen buying 1,200 June Australian dollars and selling nearby Canadian dollars, which pushed that contract down to the day's low, brokers said.
Traders said the Canadian dollar looked poised for further losses, based on its weak technical performance.
"The Canadian dollar is disappointing," said one bank floor broker. "It looks like it's going to test the 1.40 level."

But June Mexican peso rose to a new contract high at $0.123475, above the old peak at $0.123300, on what brokers said were capital inflows to take advantage of high Mexican rates. Overnight Mexican interest rates had climbed sharply Wednesday but edged back down Thursday to 24.60 percent, off some 90 basis points from Wednesday's close.
A Canadian-owned bank late bought some 300 September and December peso, boosting nearby June as well, brokers said.

Yen had eroded during the afternoon, pressured mainly by technical selling after futures broke below support near $0.008005 and hit sellstops near the overnight low of $0.008004, also roughly 126.00 spot.
But selling petered out and left next support intact near $0.007994. Brokers looked for more support at $0.007981.

Brokers glossed over more comments by U.S. Federal Reserve officials. Kansas City Fed president Thomas Hoenig said the Fed has an "obligation" to preserve the dollar's value and that the economic evidence is mixed but signs suggest inflation risks "on the upside."
Fed governor Laurence Meyer said the economy is growing quite strongly, close to capacity or maybe above. He also warned of the inflation risks from pushing U.S. unemployment down too far.
Marks gained ground early after Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said the mark's current level reflected fundamentals but that the Bundesbank was not interested in the mark weakening further.
He also said Bundesbank will watch U.S. rate moves closely but make its own decisions and that he did not see a rise or a cut in German interest rates in the foreseeable future.
June marks, however, stalled at the overnight peak of $0.5835 and drifted much of the balance of the day.

June yen ended off $0.000019 at $0.008004, marks rose $0.0014 to $0.5824, Swiss francs gained $0.0024 to $0.6864, sterling rose $0.0058 to $1.6288, Canadian dollar lost $0.0022 to $0.7169, Aussie dollar rose $0.0044 to $0.7760, Mexican peso jumped $0.000475 to $0.123400.
